rationale: The item asks whether fear has made the respondent put off making a dental appointment -> this is dental visit avoidance behavior that involves delay in scheduling a dental appointment (OHD_0005012) -> OHD_0008024 is defined as a question about that behavior, and it is the most specific class on the avoidance branch, so its ancestors (OHD_0008022, OHD_0008021, OHD_0008020, OHD_0008007) are excluded; the ontology states only that avoidance 'precedes only' a dental visit, not 'precedes some', so 'process before dental visit' (OHD_0008041) cannot be inferred.

The item asks whether dental fear led the respondent to cancel or not show up for an appointment, so it is about OHD_0005013 (dental visit avoidance behavior that involves canceling or not showing up for a dental appointment); OHD_0008023 is defined as a question about exactly that, and it is the most specific class on that branch, so its ancestors (dental visit avoidance, health encounter avoidance, avoidance behavior, and avoidance or anticipatory fear questions) are dropped.

The item asks about muscles becoming tense -> EMRO_0000010 muscle tension response to emotion is a muscle contraction, which is a muscle system process and therefore a GO_0003008 system process -> OHD_0008047 question about physiological arousal is defined as a question about some system process; nothing in the item places it before, during or after a dental visit, so no visit-timing class applies.

The item asks about an increase in breathing rate, which maps to EMRO_0000012 (increased breathing rate response to emotion); this is a respiratory system process, a kind of system process (GO_0003008), and question about physiological arousal is defined as a question about some system process, while no more specific subclass such as embarrassment applies.

The item asks about perspiring as a fear response -> sweat secretion response to emotion is a sweat secretion, which is a secretion by tissue -> question about physiological arousal is defined as a question about some secretion by tissue. No during-visit class is assigned because the item text does not mention a dental visit.

The item asks about feeling nauseated and sick to the stomach -> nausea (OHD_0008051) is a pathological bodily process (OGMS_0000061) -> question about physiological arousal (OHD_0008047) is defined as a question about some system process, secretion by tissue, or pathological bodily process; the ontology does not tie nausea to any dental-visit timing or other class.

The item asks about an increased heart rate, which is EMRO_0000011 (increased heart response to emotion); that is a heart process, which is a circulatory system process, which is a system process (GO_0003008), so the item satisfies question about physiological arousal (OHD_0008047); no subclass (embarrassment) applies and the item does not state when it happens relative to a dental visit.

The item asks about fear when making a dental appointment, which happens before the visit -> process before dental visit (OHD_0008037) -> question about prior to dental visit (OHD_0008041); scheduling is not itself avoidance, so no avoidance class applies, and the item belongs to the DFS anticipatory/avoidance item list -> avoidance or anticipatory fear question (OHD_0008007).

The item asks about fear while approaching the dentist's office, which happens before the visit begins -> this is a process before dental visit (precedes some dental visit) -> question about prior to dental visit; I also assign the avoidance or anticipatory fear question class because this Dental Fear Survey item is usually listed in that subscale, though Part 3 does not give the item list, so this assignment cannot be checked against the ontology.

The item asks about the patient sitting in the waiting room (OHD_0008027), a process during a dental visit, so it satisfies 'question about patient sitting in a waiting room' (OHD_0008029); separately, assuming this is the DFS item of that wording, its place in the DFS avoidance/anticipatory fear subscale item list also makes it an 'avoidance or anticipatory fear question' (OHD_0008007), which sits on an unrelated branch.

The item asks about sitting in the dental chair, which is a sitting process in which the patient, in the dental patient role, takes part during a dental visit; that makes it a process during dental visit, so the item fits question about during dental visit (OHD_0008042). It is not the waiting-room sitting concept and not a dental procedure itself, so no more specific class applies. The item also matches the Dental Fear Survey item 'Being seated in the dental chair', which, on my recall of the standard factor structure rather than any item list given here, belongs to the avoidance/anticipatory fear subscale (OHD_0008007), whose membership is set by item list rather than content.

The item is DFS item 12, about anticipatory fear triggered by the smell of the dentist's office, and the avoidance or anticipatory fear class is defined by DFS item membership; in the commonly reported DFS factor structure (avoidance/anticipatory anxiety = items 1, 2 and 8-13, specific stimuli = 14-20, arousal = 3-7) item 12 falls in that subscale, though some factor solutions differ, and a smell is not a process during the visit, a dental procedure or a physiological response, so no Part 2 concept applies.

The item asks about the patient seeing the dentist enter, which is a process during a dental visit in which the patient takes part (OHD_0008039), so it is a question about during dental visit (OHD_0008042); it is also mapped to the avoidance/anticipatory fear subscale (OHD_0008007) on the assumption that this Dental Fear Survey item (item 13 in the standard numbering) belongs to that subscale's item list rather than the specific-stimuli list (needle and drill items), although the item list itself is not given here.

The item is the Dental Fear Survey item about seeing the anesthetic needle, which belongs to the DFS fear-of-specific-dental-stimuli subscale (needle, injection, drill sight, sound and vibration) -> OHD_0008046 is defined by that fixed DFS item list -> no Part 2 concept covers seeing a needle or anesthetic injection, and the ontology does not state that this act realizes a dental patient role or is a dental procedure, so the during-visit and dental-procedure classes are not assigned.

The item is the Dental Fear Survey item 'feeling the needle injected', which belongs to the DFS specific-dental-stimuli subscale, so it is a fear of specific dental stimuli question (OHD_0008046); the injection is given by the dentist to the patient, realizing both the dental provider and dental patient roles, so it satisfies the definition of dental procedure (OHD_0000002) and makes the item a dental procedure question (OHD_0008044).

The item asks about fear when seeing the dental drill, so it is about the tooth drilling procedure (OHD_0008028), a dental procedure, which satisfies 'question about tooth drilling' (OHD_0008030); it is also assumed to fall under 'fear of specific dental stimuli question' (OHD_0008046), because in the standard Dental Fear Survey factor structure 'Seeing the drill' belongs to the specific-stimuli subscale, though Part 3 does not give that item list.

The item asks about hearing the dental drill, so it is about a tooth drilling procedure; a tooth drilling procedure is a dental procedure, so the item satisfies question about tooth drilling (which covers its ancestors, dental procedure question and question about during dental visit); 'Hearing the drill' is also a Dental Fear Survey item listed in the specific dental stimuli subscale, so it belongs to fear of specific dental stimuli question.

The item asks about feeling the drill's vibrations during treatment, which is about a tooth drilling procedure (OHD_0008028, a dental procedure), so it satisfies question about tooth drilling; the item is also on the Dental Fear Survey specific-dental-stimuli subscale list, whose membership is set by item list, so it belongs to fear of specific dental stimuli question.

The item asks about having one's teeth cleaned, which is a tooth cleaning procedure (OHD_0008034); that procedure is a dental procedure, so the item is a dental procedure question about a tooth cleaning procedure, matching OHD_0008035 (its ancestors are omitted, and the list-defined DFS subscale classes are not assigned because no item list is given).

The item asks about overall fear of having dental work done -> dental work is a dental procedure (OHD_0000002), so the item satisfies the dental procedure question (OHD_0008044, which is more specific than 'during dental visit'); it also asks about fear of undergoing a procedure, matching the text definition of fear of medical procedure question (OHD_0008054).

The item asks about anxiety felt shortly before going to the dentist -> this is a process before dental visit (OHD_0008037), which precedes a dental visit -> question about prior to dental visit (OHD_0008041) is defined as a question about some process before dental visit; the anticipatory-fear class (OHD_0008007) is not chosen because its membership is a fixed list of DFS items, and anxiety as such is not modeled as a system process here, so physiological arousal (OHD_0008047) is not chosen.

The item asks whether the respondent generally avoids going to the dentist because the experience is unpleasant. This is dental visit avoidance behavior (OHD_0005007), which is a kind of health encounter avoidance behavior and of avoidance behavior. The dental visit avoidance question is defined as a question about dental visit avoidance behavior, so it is the most specific match. Its children do not apply because the item mentions neither canceling or not showing up nor delay in scheduling. 'Prior to dental visit' cannot be inferred because the behavior only 'precedes only' a dental visit, and that does not guarantee 'precedes some'.

The item asks about nervousness in anticipation of upcoming dental visits, which is a process before a dental visit (OHD_0008037, which precedes some dental visit), so it satisfies 'question about prior to dental visit' (OHD_0008041); it is not a listed DFS item for OHD_0008007, it describes no avoidance behavior, and nervousness is not one of the Part 2 bodily-process concepts needed for physiological arousal.

The item asks about a catastrophic belief (expecting something really bad to happen) about a hypothetical dental visit. That belief is not avoidance behavior, a dental procedure, waiting-room sitting, a system process or secretion, embarrassment, or a specified pain. It is also not stated to precede, occur during, or follow an actual dental visit, so it fails the before-, during- and after-visit axioms. The two DFS classes are set by a fixed DFS item list, and this item is not on it, so no question class is satisfied.

The item asks about feeling afraid while visiting the dentist, which is a patient's experience occurring during a dental visit (OHD_0008039 process during dental visit), so it satisfies OHD_0008042 question about during dental visit; fear is not a defined Part 2 concept, the DFS-list classes are fixed by item list, and no avoidance, procedure or bodily-arousal concept is named.

The item asks about a faster heartbeat when going to the dentist, which is EMRO_0000011 increased heart response to emotion. That concept is a heart process, which is a circulatory system process, which is a GO_0003008 system process, so the item satisfies OHD_0008047 question about physiological arousal. It does not satisfy the during-dental-visit class because the ontology does not state that the heart response realizes the dental patient role.

The item asks about delaying making dental appointments, which is the concept OHD_0005012 (dental visit avoidance behavior that involves delay in scheduling a dental appointment); OHD_0008024 is defined as a question about exactly that, so it is the most specific matching class. Its ancestors (dental visit, health encounter and general avoidance questions) are excluded. OHD_0008041 is not inferred because the ontology states only that avoidance behavior 'precedes only' a dental visit, which does not imply the 'precedes some' needed for a process before a dental visit. OHD_0008007 is excluded because its membership is a fixed Dental Fear Survey item list, and this agree/disagree statement is not shown to be on that list.

The item asks about anticipatory worrying that happens before going to the dentist, which is a process before dental visit (OHD_0008037); question about prior to dental visit is defined as a question about some process before dental visit, so OHD_0008041 applies, while no avoidance, pain, or physiological concept is involved and the DFS-list classes are not determined by content.

The item asks whether going to the dentist is actively avoided, which is dental visit avoidance behavior (OHD_0005007); OHD_0008022 is defined as a question about that behavior. No more specific subclass fits because neither canceling/no-shows nor delay in scheduling is named. The 'endured with intense fear' clause is not tied by any stated axiom to a process that realizes the dental patient role, so the during-visit class is not entailed.

The item asks how long a general fear of going to the dentist has lasted (a duration criterion). No class covers this: it is not avoidance behavior, a dental procedure, physiological arousal, embarrassment, or a process tied to before, during or after a specific dental visit. The DFS-subscale classes are set by their fixed item lists, not by content, so no class is satisfied.

The item asks whether fear or avoidance of going to the dentist affects one's life, so it is about dental visit avoidance behavior (OHD_0005007), which matches the dental visit avoidance question (OHD_0008022); it also names being embarrassed about the appearance of teeth as one such effect, so it is about embarrassment (EMRO_0003002), which matches the question about embarrassment (OHD_0008085), though embarrassment appears only as an example and that second mapping is the weaker one.

The item asks about fear of a panic attack, which it describes by sweating and a pounding heart; sweating is sweat secretion response to emotion (a secretion by tissue) and a pounding heart is increased heart response to emotion (a system process), so the item satisfies the question about physiological arousal; it is not a listed DFS subscale item, and no before-, during- or after-visit process is clearly specified.

The item attributes dental fear to being self-conscious and concerned about being watched or judged by others. This matches embarrassment (EMRO_0003002), a self-conscious emotional experience of feeling awkward because of others' attention or observation. Question about embarrassment (OHD_0008085) is defined as a question about some embarrassment, and no avoidance behavior or specific dental visit process is asked about.

The item asks about anxiety over painful or uncomfortable procedures at the dentist, so it is about a dental procedure (OHD_0000002), which is a process during a dental visit; [OHD_0008044] dental procedure question is defined as a question about some dental procedure and is more specific than its parent [OHD_0008042] question about during dental visit. The fear-of-pain and fear-of-medical-procedure classes are excluded because they sit under [OHD_0008007], whose membership is a fixed list of Dental Fear Survey (DFS) items, and this item is not on that list.

The item asks how anxious the person is about feeling embarrassed or ashamed at the dentist -> embarrassment (EMRO_0003002) is a self-conscious emotional experience -> OHD_0008085 is defined as a question about some embarrassment. The 'during dental visit' class was not added because the ontology does not state that embarrassment realizes a dental patient role, which that class requires. The DFS-list classes were not added because this item is not shown to be on those lists.

The item asks about anxiety over not being in control of what happens while the patient is at the dentist. That is a process the patient takes part in during a dental visit (OHD_0008039, process during dental visit), so the item fits OHD_0008042 (question about during dental visit). No specific procedure, avoidance behavior, pain or physiological arousal is named, so no more specific class applies.

The item asks about anxiety over feeling sick or queasy, which is nausea; nausea is a pathological bodily process, and the physiological arousal question class is defined as a question about some pathological bodily process, while the ontology does not state that nausea is a process during a dental visit and disgust has no matching concept.

The item asks about anxiety over numbness from the anesthetic, which the patient experiences while undergoing care at the dentist. That makes it a process during dental visit (OHD_0008039: realizes the dental patient role and happens during a dental visit), so it fits the question class 'question about during dental visit'. Other classes were excluded: numbness is not among the listed system processes, secretions or pathological processes, and the item asks about the effect, not a specific dental procedure. The DFS-list classes do not apply because this is not a DFS item.

The item asks about anxiety over not knowing what the dentist is going to do during the visit, i.e. about an unspecified dental procedure (OHD_0000002) -> a dental procedure is a process during a dental visit -> dental procedure question (OHD_0008044) is defined as a question about some dental procedure and is the most specific class, so its ancestor 'question about during dental visit' is not listed separately.

The item asks about anxiety over the financial cost of dental treatment. Cost is not a dental procedure, an avoidance behavior, a physiological process or a stated before/during/after-visit process in Part 2, so no question class definition is satisfied.

The item asks about anxiety over needles or injections at the dentist. Injections are given during dental treatment, so they are best covered by dental procedure (OHD_0000002), which happens during a dental visit. Class OHD_0008044 is defined as a question about some dental procedure, and it is more specific than 'question about during dental visit'. I did not use the fear-of-dental-stimuli or fear-of-medical-procedure classes. They sit under DFS item-list subscales, and this item is not a DFS item.

The item asks about anxiety over gagging or choking that occurs while the patient is at the dentist, which is a process during the dental visit (OHD_0008039), and question about during dental visit (OHD_0008042) is defined as a question about such a process; gagging is not a listed concept, so it cannot be linked to nausea or physiological arousal, and the DFS-list classes do not apply because this is not a listed DFS item.

The item asks about anxiety over the dentist's unkind or unsympathetic manner while the patient is at the dentist. That is an encounter in which the patient is under the dentist's care, so it realizes the dental patient role during a dental visit and counts as a process during dental visit (OHD_0008039), which makes it a question about during dental visit (OHD_0008042). No specific dental procedure, avoidance behavior or physiological reaction is mentioned, and the item is not on the fixed DFS subscale lists, so no more specific class applies.

The item asks how the respondent feels the day before a dental treatment visit, which is anticipatory feeling -> a process before dental visit (OHD_0008037) -> class OHD_0008041 is defined as a question about a process before dental visit; OHD_0008007 is excluded because its membership is a fixed list of Dental Fear Survey items, not set by content.

The item asks how the respondent feels while sitting in the waiting room before treatment -> it is about OHD_0008027 'patient sitting in waiting room' -> OHD_0008029 is defined as a question about some patient sitting in waiting room. That concept is also a subclass of 'process during dental visit', so OHD_0008029's ancestor OHD_0008042 is satisfied too and is dropped in favour of the more specific class.

The item asks how the respondent would feel about having a tooth drilled -> tooth drilling procedure (OHD_0008028) is a dental procedure, which is a process during a dental visit -> OHD_0008030 is defined as a dental procedure question about some tooth drilling procedure, so it is the most specific match; the anticipatory-fear branch (OHD_0008007) is excluded because its membership is a fixed list of Dental Fear Survey items, not set by content.

The item asks how the respondent would feel about having teeth scaled and polished -> tooth scaling and tooth polishing procedures are both a tooth cleaning procedure, which is a dental procedure -> OHD_0008035 is defined as a dental procedure question about some tooth cleaning procedure, and it subsumes the dental procedure and during-dental-visit classes; the anticipatory-fear branch is not chosen because its membership is a fixed list of Dental Fear Survey items, not set by content.

The item asks how the patient would feel about undergoing a local anaesthetic injection in the gum, which is a dental procedure (OHD_0000002, a process during a dental visit) -> dental procedure question (OHD_0008044) is defined as a question about some dental procedure and is more specific than 'question about during dental visit'; 'fear of medical procedure question' was excluded because its parent 'avoidance or anticipatory fear question' is restricted to a fixed list of Dental Fear Survey items, and this item is not shown to be on that list.
